questions.q: What does a Power Platform environment isolate?
options: Nothing — all environments in a tenant share the same apps, flows, and data
Only Dataverse data, but apps and flows are shared across environments
Apps, flows, connections, and an optional Dataverse database, all separate from every other environment
Only user licenses
questions.explain: An environment is a hard boundary: everything built or connected inside it — apps, flows, connections, and an optional Dataverse database — is isolated from other environments, even within the same tenant.

questions.q: Which environment type is specifically designed for development and testing, with support for copy and reset operations?
options: Default
Sandbox
Trial
Production
questions.explain: Sandbox environments are non-production environments meant for development and testing, and they support copying data in from Production or resetting the environment.

questions.q: Why shouldn't Castlebridge build and test new flows directly in its Production environment?
options: Production environments don't allow any flow creation at all
A broken condition or bad query would hit live shipment data immediately, with no safety net
Flows run slower in Production than in Dev
Production environments can't contain a Dataverse database
questions.explain: Building directly in Production means mistakes affect real, live data immediately. Dev and Test environments exist to catch problems before they can reach the business.

questions.q: What is the Default environment primarily used for?
options: Hosting Castlebridge's production shipment-tracking flows
Automated, short-term testing that expires after 30 days
Lightweight experimentation — it's auto-created per tenant, shared by all licensed users, with no backup guarantees
Running the company's most critical, business-dependent automation
questions.explain: The Default environment is created automatically for every tenant and shared by all users. It's meant for experimentation, not serious or production workloads, and has no backup guarantees.

questions.q: In Castlebridge's three-environment strategy, what is the correct order a flow moves through before reaching users?
options: Production, then Test, then Dev
Dev, then Production, then Test
Test, then Dev, then Production
Dev, then Test, then Production
questions.explain: A flow is built in Dev, exported as a solution, imported into Test for validation, and only then imported into Production — using environment variables and connection references to repoint it at each stop.
